To ensure you never miss a transaction update, please keep your personal details and email records up to date. Go to Trust App > Profile > Settings > Personal details to get started!

question: Why am I not allowed to use a nickname for my PayNow name?
answer: - The Association of Banks in Singapore as the PayNow scheme owner regularly reviews measures to improve the security of digital payments. The discontinuation of PayNow’s nickname feature for retail customers is intended to combat impersonation scams. The nickname feature has been available since PayNow’s launch in 2017, originally introduced to address privacy concerns from individuals who preferred not to display their full registered names when receiving payments via their mobile numbers or NRIC numbers. However, scammers have exploited this privacy feature. They would register PayNow accounts and then set a nickname to mirror those of legitimate companies or individuals they sought to impersonate. This enabled them to create convincing facades when soliciting payments or when victims were verifying transfer details. By removing the nickname feature, the system will only display verified, registered account names, significantly reducing scammers' ability to masquerade as legitimate entities or individuals. This change forces greater transparency in payment identification, making it considerably more difficult for scammers to successfully impersonate trusted organisations or individuals through manipulated account names.

question: What display name will replace the nickname?
answer: - Under the enhanced security framework, instead of displaying nicknames or full account names, selected letters of a retail Payee’s registered account name with their financial institution will be displayed to the Payer during PayNow transfers. This measure will ensure that only registered account names are displayed as the Payee’s PayNow name. Impersonation scams can be mitigated with this new measure, which offers Payers greater confidence as to whom they would be transferring funds to. To address concerns from individuals who do not wish to reveal their full registered names and safeguard their privacy as Payees, only selected letters of the Payee’s name will be displayed to Payer. The partial display of names also prevents full disclosure of the registered name and provides protection against name harvesting through PayNow's lookup feature. By anchoring the display to verified, registered account names rather than user-selected nicknames, this measure significantly reduces scammers' ability to masquerade as legitimate entities whilst maintaining user privacy through selected character display. Payers can now have greater confidence in the authenticity of transfer recipients, as the displayed information is tied directly to officially registered account details rather than deceptive customised nicknames.

question: How will it improve security issues?
answer: - The proposed change will reduce the scammers' ability to masquerade as legitimate entities or persons to deceive unsuspecting users through PayNow transactions.

question: What will my masked name look like?
answer: - From 6 June 2026 onwards, payor's will only be able to see their payee’s registered account name with only selected letters displayed, before making a transfer or payment. For illustration purposes, please refer to the following examples shared by ABS:

question: How will this change impact me?
answer: - No action is needed on your part. All other aspects of receiving and transferring money via PayNow remain unchanged. Individuals and corporates can continue to pay to your PayNow proxies (mobile number, NRIC/FIN, or VPA) as before. From 6 June 2026, Payers making payment to you via PayNow will be shown selected letters of your Payee’s name during a PayNow transfer.

question: Why can’t I set a nickname for my PayNow registration?
answer: - PayNow’s nickname option will be removed starting 6 June 2026. Instead, a masked version of your registered account name will be displayed as your PayNow name.

question: I do not have a PayNow nickname, how will I be impacted?
answer: - Without a nickname, your registered account name is displayed in full to your Payers today. From 6 June 2026, only selected letters of your account name will be displayed. There is no action required on your part.

question: What happens to my current PayNow nickname?
answer: - Your existing PayNow proxy details will be automatically updated with your PayNow name displaying selected letters of your registered account name with your financial institution starting 6 Jun 2026. There is no action required on your part.

question: Do I need to take any actions on my current PayNow registrations?
answer: - No. There is no action required from you as the changes will be managed by Trust and the PayNow scheme operator.

question: If anyone enters my PayNow proxy to make a payment, what will they see?
answer: - Once the name changes take effect, your payors will see the masked name as and when they enter your PayNow proxy to make payment.

question: Can I define what characters of my name need to be masked?
answer: - The logic for the updated PayNow name has taken into consideration industry best practices, consumer feedback, and is centrally applied to provide consistency. Hence, users will not be able to make changes to the updated PayNow name.

question: How do I know if my updated PayNow name is correct?
answer: - Trust and the PayNow scheme operator financial will update your PayNow name based on your registered account name record. Hence, you can be assured that due diligence will be done to ensure that your updated PayNow name is correct.

question: When I make a PayNow payment to a company (e.g. Scan & Pay), should the company name be masked?
answer: - No, Corporate PayNow names will not be masked.

question: Do I need to take any actions for my child’s PayNow registrations?
answer: - No. There is no action required from you as the changes will be managed by the PayNow scheme operator and Trust.

question: What will I see when I am transferring funds as a Payer?
answer: - If you are transferring funds to a retail Payee, upon entering the Payee’s PayNow proxy to make payment, you will only see selected letters of the Payee’s name as their updated PayNow name. If you are transferring funds to a corporate Payee, there is no change and you will see the full registered account name of the company as per today. The above apply for all PayNow payment transfers initiated by you, including through Scan to Pay.

question: Why is my full name as a Payer being shown in full to my Payees?
answer: - The display of selected letters of a retail user’s PayNow name only applies when you are a Payee and recipient of payments. This is one of the many measures adopted to help combat impersonation scams and to safeguard customer privacy for Payees. As a Payer, your full account name will be shown in your Payee’s financial institution’s statement and transaction records. This is currently how it is displayed and there is no change. The display of full account names of Payers is a standard practice across major payment schemes and supports a broad set of business use cases that require validation of a Payer’s identity (e.g. brokerages that need to validate that investment funds came from a first party). It is also useful in cases of disputes and aid identification of potential scams or fraud where Payees can raise queries to their financial institutions on funds transferred into their accounts from unknown Payers.

question: What is Trust?
answer: - Trust Bank (known as Trust) is a digitally-native bank, backed by a unique partnership between Standard Chartered Bank and FairPrice Group. This partnership brings together a leading international bank and a social enterprise with more than 200 years of combined experience in Singapore.

question: What's the story behind the name Trust?

It also reflects the values with which we have built our bank and the standing of our shareholders in Singapore. The “us” in “Trust” also represents how we are a bank for all in Singapore – bringing all of us together!

question: How is a digitally-native bank different from other banks?
answer: - Trust is designed and built to operate entirely on your mobile phone, using the latest and best technology. We focus on digitising as many of the traditional processes as possible, we don’t have any branches and we operate 24/7. This allows us to deliver a banking service to you that we hope is easier and faster to use. Our sign-up process is a great example of this as it takes just a couple of minutes for Singapore residents using Singpass.

question: I already bank with Standard Chartered. Does that mean I automatically get a Trust account?
answer: - No, but that’s okay. You can sign up for a Trust account on your mobile in just a few minutes and immediately enjoy savings on your everyday spending.

question: How do I sign up for a Trust account?
answer: - All you need is your mobile phone and MyInfo authentication to pre-fill your application quickly and securely! In addition, foreigners residing in Singapore will need to upload a copy of your passport and income documents (for credit card applications).

question: Is my money safe with Trust?

question: Can I apply for a Trust account via the Trust app if I am overseas?

question: What is MyInfo and why should I use it during sign up?

question: When I am redirected to Singpass app to authenticate myself, will I be able to login via the Singpass username and password option?

question: How do I update my personal information (address, phone number, email) with Trust?

question: Can I cancel my update request after submission?
answer: - No, you will not be able to cancel your request once it’s submitted. However, you can simply re-submit another update request 12 hours later for phone number & email, or instantly for address.

question: Will my old phone number used for PayNow be automatically deregistered once I update to a new phone number?

question: Where do I receive my one-time password (“OTP”) when I manually add my card to Google Wallet or Google Pay?

question: How long is my OTP valid for?

question: I did not receive my OTP sent by Trust. What should I do?

question: What if I exit the app while applying for a Trust account?

question: How do I know that the email I have received is from Trust Bank?

question: Why is Android Debug Bridge (ADB) not allowed?
answer: - For security reasons, the Trust App does not allow usage on mobile devices with Android Debug Bridge (ADB) enabled, as ADB can pose a risk to your privacy and app security. To continue using the Trust App, please disable ADB in your device’s settings.

question: What does TrustInvest Mutual Funds offer?
answer: - We offer a set of 9 mutual funds curated specially for our customers.

question: Are there any requirements to open a TrustInvest Mutual Funds account?
answer: - Yes, you need a Trust savings account before you can open a TrustInvest Mutual Funds account. Download Trust App to open a Trust savings account if you do not have one yet.

question: How do I start investing?
answer: - If you meet our requirements, you will be able to view an Invest section on your Trust App home screen. Simply tap on it and click on Mutual Funds to open your TrustInvest Mutual Funds account! Do note that your eligibility to invest will be subject to the Trust's internal assessment.

question: What fees will I be charged?
answer: - Trust doesn’t have any platform fees or sales charges. The management fee, charged by the fund manager, is already accounted for in the fund’s price (net asset value). A portion of this fee is paid to Trust. The fund also incurs other operating costs (e.g. custody, administration costs) which are likewise factored into the fund’s price. You can refer to the Total Expense Ratio (TER) in the fund documents which is an indication of the all-in annual cost of running the fund. This is expressed as a percentage of the fund’s assets.

question: Is my capital protected when investing?
answer: - No, a mutual fund is an investment product and not a bank deposit. Investments in mutual funds are not capital protected. All investment products involve risks, including the possible loss of all or part of your original investment amount. Fund valuations and returns may go up or down and are not guaranteed. Past performance is not indicative of future performance.

question: Who can apply for the TrustInvest Mutual Funds account?
answer: - You may apply for the TrustInvest Mutual Funds account if: - You have an existing Trust savings account. - You are between 18 and 74 years old. Note that US persons are ineligible to open a TrustInvest Mutual Funds account.

question: Why am I missing the Investments section in Trust App?
answer: - Only eligible customers can see the Investment section in Trust App. Please ensure that you are using the latest version of Trust App. Need help? Please contact us via the in-app chat or call us at +65 313-TRUST (+65 3138 7878).

question: What is the minimum investment amount?
answer: - The minimum investment amount for Mutual Funds is S$100 per order, except for PIMCO GIS Income Fund SGD-Hedged (Dist.) where the minimum investment is S$1,500.

question: What is the difference between TrustInvest Mutual Funds account and Trust savings account?
answer: - The TrustInvest Mutual Funds account is solely used for investing. This account is non-interest bearing and cannot be used for other banking purposes. Monies in the TrustInvest Mutual Funds account are not insured by the Singapore Deposit Insurance Corporation (SDIC), whereas monies in Trust savings account is insured by SDIC.

question: Where are my investment monies held?
answer: - Your monies and assets are held with our custodian in accordance with the Securities and Futures Act.

question: Is there interest earned on my TrustInvest Mutual Funds account?
answer: - No, the cash balance in your TrustInvest Mutual Funds Account will not earn interest.

question: Does Trust provide investment advice?
answer: - No, Trust does not provide any investment advice to customers.

question: Can I use CPF/SRS account to fund my investments?
answer: - Unfortunately, CPF/SRS investments will not be available at the moment.

question: What is the Management Fee Rebate Programme?
answer: - The Trust's Management Fee Rebate Programme is introduced to reduce the cost of long-term investing for our customers. This is achieved by rebating a portion of the management fee to clients who stay invested with us till the end of the year.

question: How does the Management Fee Rebate programme work?
answer: - The rebate promotion period is from 1 January 2025 - 31 December 2025. Rebates are calculated and accrued daily based on your end of day position in each fund. answer: - Split Purchase allows you to split eligible transactions into a fixed number of equal monthly payments for a one-time fee. We will charge a one-time fee which will depend on the total amount, the number of monthly payments and your personal credit profile.

question: Why do I need to wait for 12 hours before my transaction limit is increased or before a new payee is added?
answer: - Adding a new payee or requesting a transaction limit increase will only be effective after a 12-hour cooling off period. This provides an extra layer of security by preventing large sums from being transferred immediately if the transaction limit was increased to send funds to a scammer suspicious payee. However, if you want to reduce your existing transaction limit, it will take effect immediately.

question: When will I experience the 12-hour cooling off period for increasing my transaction limit?
answer: - You will experience the cooling off period immediately after you submit your request to increase your transaction limit. Once we receive your request, we will send a push notification and an email to your registered email address. If you receive these notifications but did not submit the request, please contact us immediately. If you have an ongoing request to increase your limit, any new request to increase your transaction limit will overwrite your ongoing request. The new request will only take effect after 12 hours from the time of receiving the new request.

question: When will the 12-hour cooling off period take effect for adding a new payee?
answer: - Once we receive your request to add a new payee, this payee will be subject to a 12-hour cooling period and added after 12 hours. We will send a push notification and an email to your registered email address. If you receive these notifications but did not submit the request, please contact us immediately. During the cooling off period, you will not be able to make a transfer to the newly added payee.

question: Will I be able to make a transaction in Trust App during the 12-hour cooling period?
answer: - Yes, you can still make a transaction that is within your existing transaction limit during the cooling off period.

question: Will I be able to transfer funds to the newly added payee during the 12-hour cooling off period?
answer: - No, you will not be able to make transfer(s) to the payee during the cooling off period.

question: Do I need to return money that has been incorrectly transferred into my account? Can I refuse to do so?

question: How can I review and update my existing transaction limit?

question: Is there a service charge for transferring money to/from my Savings Account by Trust?
answer: - No, it is absolutely free to transfer in Singapore dollars and receive Singapore dollars into your Savings Account by Trust.

question: How long does it take to process a local transfer request?
answer: - Your local transfer will be sent in real time to the recipient and you'll receive an immediate confirmation. However, the receiving bank may take some time to process and settle the request.

question: Can I transfer money in foreign currency?
answer: - Currently, we only accept local SGD transfers. We do not support inward and outward transfers of foreign currencies or cross-border payments (in either SGD or foreign currencies).

question: How do I check if I have set Trust as my PayNow registered bank?
answer: - You can check your PayNow registrations in a few easy steps: - Log into your Trust App - Tap on Savings -> Payments - Tap on “…” - Select the PayNow registration option

question: I'm a foreigner so I don't have a Singapore NRIC. Can I use my FIN or passport to register for PayNow?
answer: - You can register your FIN or mobile number for PayNow with Trust, but not with your passport number as it's not supported for PayNow.

question: Can I use an international mobile number to register for PayNow?
answer: - You can register only Singapore mobile numbers for PayNow.

question: I registered both my NRIC and mobile number for PayNow. If I delete my NRIC for PayNow, will my mobile number be deleted as well?
answer: - Only the linkage of the account to your NRIC will be deleted and you'll no longer be able to receive funds via your NRIC with PayNow. Your registered mobile number remains unaffected and you can continue to receive funds via your mobile number with PayNow.

question: Can I change my display name after registration?
answer: - Of course, you may do so via your Trust App!

question: What must I do if I change my mobile number after linking it to my Savings Account by Trust for PayNow?
answer: - You can register your new mobile number for PayNow in 3 easy steps: 1. De-register your old mobile no. via Trust App. 2. Update your new mobile number. 3. Re-register your new mobile number for PayNow by linking it to your Savings Account by Trust.

question: Do I need to add a payee before making a transfer via PayNow / Scan & Pay or can I perform ad hoc transfers? Is there a transfer limit?
answer: - For transfer amount of S$ 5000 or less, you can perform the transfer without adding a payee. For transfer amount between S$ 5000 and S$ 200,000, you would need to add the recipient as a payee first or perform additional verification using the Trust Key before the transfer.

question: How will my PayNow transfers appear on my account statements?
answer: - All your PayNow transfers will be recorded in your account statements with transaction descriptions containing the recipient's name.

question: Can I use PayNow to transfer funds to my overseas bank accounts?
answer: - No, PayNow can only be used for SGD funds transfers between FAST participating banks in Singapore.

question: I have linked my account with another bank to my mobile number (or NRIC) to receive funds via PayNow. Can I link the same mobile number to my Trust Account for PayNow?
answer: - Yes, you can. However, before you do so you must first delete the existing link between your mobile number (or NRIC) and your account with the other bank.

question: Can I cancel a local transfer?
answer: - No, you can’t cancel once you’ve confirmed a transfer. Be sure to double-check that you have the right recipient and transfer amount before you confirm a transfer.

question: How can I avoid transferring funds to the wrong recipient?
answer: - Make sure you review and double-check all payment details before tapping 'Confirm'.

question: Will my payments/transfers be eligible for spend bonus interest for my Savings Account by Trust?
answer: - No, payments/transfers are not eligible when considering spend bonus interest eligibility for your Savings Account by Trust. Only debit and/or credit card spends are considered as qualifying transactions to earn spend bonus interest on savings account.

question: How can I change my transfer limits?
answer: - To change your Bank Transfer limits, simply log into the Trust App, then tap on ‘Money’ then ‘Payments’ then ‘…’ to set your preferred limit. Once this is done, tap on ‘confirm new limit’. For increase in limits, you will need to perform additional verification using the Trust Key.

question: What is the Transfer Limit for PayNow and FAST?
answer: - For PayNow or FAST transfer to added payees (to third party accounts within Trust and other banks’ accounts/cards) the maximum transfer limit is S$ 200,000 per transaction and S$ 200,000 for overall daily limit. For PayNow to non-added payees, the default transfer limit daily is S$ 5000 and additional verification using the Trust Key is required for amounts more than S$ 5000.

question: How can I set up a GIRO arrangement?
answer: - We do not support the set up of GIRO arrangements at the moment. Please stay tuned.

question: Does my Trust savings account support eGIRO?
answer: - We do not support eGIRO at the moment. Please stay tuned.

question: How can I deposit/issue a cheque?
answer: - We do not support cheque at the moment. Please stay tuned.

question: How can I submit a GIRO form to arrange for bill payments?

question: How can I receive government payouts into my Trust savings account?
answer: - You may receive the funds to your savings account by registering your NRIC for PayNow with Trust.

question: Can I set up Trust savings account as the receiving account to credit my salary?
answer: - Yes, you may inform your organisation to credit your salary to your Trust savings account. Trust bank can now process incoming salary payments.

question: Can I receive funds into my Trust savings account on a regular basis?
answer: - a) Yes, you can set up recurring local funds transfer, also known as Standing Instructions and Scheduled Transfers from other banks to your designated Trust savings account for receiving funds on a regular basis. b) You may indicate the payment frequency, amount and receiving account number using the banking channels from other banks.

question: Can I make a local funds transfer (non-FAST) to my Trust savings account?
answer: - Yes, you can initiate a local funds transfer via GIRO from other banks to your designated Trust savings account. However, transfers via MEPS+ or RTGS are not supported.

question: Can I transfer money on a regular basis to other bank accounts?

question: How do I disable my AutoPay?
answer: - For Trust credit card AutoPay, you may disable AutoPay by following the steps below: - Log in to your Trust App - Tap on ‘Pay card’ on your credit card tab - Tap on ‘View’ on AutoPay tab - Tap on ‘Disable AutoPay’ Do note that if your savings account is closed, the scheduled AutoPay would be automatically cancelled and no payment would be executed For Trust savings pot AutoPay, you may disable AutoPay by following the steps below: - Log in to your Trust App - Tap on the savings pot that you would like to disable - Tap on ‘AutoPay’ tab - Tap on ‘Delete this AutoPay’ Do note that if you break your Trust savings pot, the scheduled AutoPay would also be automatically cancelled and no scheduled transfer would be executed. question: Can I edit the fields I have selected for AutoPay?
answer: - Yes. You may amend the fields for AutoPay via Bank Transfer / PayNow / Saving Pots via the following steps: - Tap on ‘AutoPay’ then select the AutoPay that you want to edit - Tap on ‘Edit’ - Fields that you can edit are Amount, End Date, Frequency - Tap on ‘Confirm’ For Trust credit card AutoPay, you may do so by disabling the existing AutoPay and setting up a new AutoPay by indicating the new repayment amount type of your choice. question: Can I choose my preferred scheduled payment date for AutoPay?
answer: - For paying your Trust credit card from Trust savings account: No, AutoPay schedule is fixed at 2 days before your payment due date every month. For other types of AutoPay: Yes, you can select your preferred scheduled payment date when you set up AutoPay. For savings pot, the frequencies that you can select are Weekly, Monthly and Quarterly. question: What are the E-Payments User Protection Guidelines?
answer: - The E-Payments User Protection Guidelines issued by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) set out the duties of responsible financial institutions and consumers in relation to unauthorised and erroneous payment transactions in relation to protected accounts, and provides guidance on the liability for losses arising from unauthorised transactions. A “protected account” means any payment account that— (a) is held in the name of one or more persons, all of whom are either individuals or sole proprietors; (b) is capable of having a balance of more than S$1,000 (or equivalent amount expressed in any other currency) at any one time, or is a credit facility; (c) is capable of being used for electronic payment transactions; and (d) where issued by a relevant payment service provider is a payment account that stores specified e-money. Under the Guidelines, the account holder of a protected account should perform duties including: - download mobile applications only from official sources and update browser and operating systems regularly, - provide accurate and complete contact information, opt to receive all outgoing transaction notifications and monitor notifications, - protect One-Time-Passwords (OTP) sent via App / SMS and secure access to protected account, - read content including risk warning messages sent by the Bank before completing payment transactions or high-risk activities, - refer to official sources to obtain website addresses and phone numbers, - understand the risks and implications of performing high-risk activities, - report any unauthorised activities on his protected account, activate self-service feature (“kill switch”) provided by the Bank promptly to block further mobile and online access to the protected account, and provide information to the Bank on unauthorised transactions, and - make police report to facilitate the Bank’s claims investigation process, or if the account holder suspects that he is a victim of scam or fraud. You can access the full E-Payment Guidelines from MAS at the link below. https://www.mas.gov.sg/regulation/guidelines/e-payments-user-protection-guidelines

question: Why don’t I see my bus/mrt transaction on my app after tapping out from the bus/mrt gantry?
